title: 10ftv8x
Saqifa of Banu Sa'ida and the process of bay'a
hook: While the Prophet's body was still being washed, the bay'a was taken at Saqifa. The Ahl al-Bayt were left alone at the funeral.
scenes.0.text: In Medina the Prophet had just passed away. **Imam Ali**, whose hand had been raised at Ghadir, was at his bedside. The news of the death threw the city into turmoil. Imam Ali set about preparing the washing and burial with Abbas and the Banu Hashim. He did not leave the side of the body.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: qhlvls
Banu Hashim
scenes.1.text: In those same hours the Ansar gathered in the shade of Banu Sa'ida. The sick Sa'd b. Ubada was there too. They wanted the leadership to be from among themselves. The Prophet's body had not yet been washed. In this gathering, the right proclaimed for **Imam Ali** at Ghadir was not discussed.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 13r2a44
The Ansar
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: arlxb3
Sa'd b. Ubada
scenes.2.text: Upon hearing the news, Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubayda ran to **Saqifa**. Abu Bakr first praised the Ansar. Then he said that the Arabs would not give leadership to anyone other than the Quraysh. **Imam Ali**'s hand had been raised at Ghadir. In this gathering, that proclamation was disregarded.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 13r2a44
The Ansar
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.2.art.actors.2.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.2.art.actors.3.label: 1suddrx
Abu Ubayda
scenes.3.text: At **Saqifa**, Hubab said, "an amir from us, an amir from you." Bashir spoke in favor of the Quraysh. Voices rose. The old rivalry of the Aws and the Khazraj intervened. The bay'a, that is, the pledge of allegiance, was determined not by the proclamation at Ghadir but by this tribal contention.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 18o1s5l
Hubab b. Mundhir
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 1adi38t
Bashir b. Sa'd
scenes.4.text: At **Saqifa**, Umar took Abu Bakr's hand and pledged allegiance. Others followed. The atmosphere grew so tense that it was said, "You have killed Sa'd." Sa'd did not pledge allegiance. **Imam Ali**, meanwhile, was still at the washing of the Prophet.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.5.text: Years later, Caliph Umar called this bay'a a "falta." A falta is a decision taken in haste, without consultation. He said God had averted its evil. He said it must not be repeated. That hasty decision pushed aside the right proclaimed at Ghadir. The matter had been finished on one afternoon of the day of the death.
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.6.text: Imam Ali did not pledge allegiance. For six months he stood by his wife **Lady Fatima** in her grief. Fadak was seized. A threat of fire had been sworn before Lady Fatima's door. When Lady Fatima passed away, Imam Ali kept his silence so that no blood would be shed and the Ummah would not be divided. He was silent for the sake of peace. He did not forget his right at Ghadir.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.7.text: After Lady Fatima's passing, people's attitude toward Imam Ali changed. Bukhari 4240 relates that Imam Ali found the faces of the people unfamiliar. This hadith was cited only for this coldness. The same hadith then also records that Imam Ali pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr. The Shia reading in the app does not count that continuation as accepted. According to reports, **Imam Ali** would give the greeting in the street. People would not return his greeting.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.8.text: At night Medina fell silent. According to reports, **Imam Ali** would go alone to the edge of the well. The surroundings were empty. He would put his hands on the rim of the well. His sorrow was there. **Lady Fatima** was gone. People had turned their faces away. The loneliness was heavy. He had not forgotten his right at Ghadir. He had lowered his voice so that no blood would be shed. He would pour out his heart to the well. When morning came he would return to the city. His face was calm. His burden remained.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.9.text: Then Caliph Umar left the matter to a council of six. The shura is a consultative council. The bay'a was given to Uthman. In the Shiqshiqiyya sermon, **Imam Ali** recalls these days with patience. The setting aside of the right, which began at Saqifa, continued at the shura as well. His patience was not the forgetting of the right.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: 18i2n4z
Abd al-Rahman b. Awf
scenes.9.art.actors.2.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
sunni.0.says: Caliph Umar's long sermon: that the bay'a of Caliph Abu Bakr was a "falta," that God averted its evil, that it must not be repeated; the debate and tension at Saqifa.
sunni.1.says: Lady Fatima asks Caliph Abu Bakr for her inheritance; she is refused, Lady Fatima becomes estranged and passes away six months later; Imam Ali buries her at night. That while Lady Fatima was alive people held Imam Ali in esteem, and after her passing Imam Ali found the faces of the people unfamiliar, is also in this hadith. It then records that Imam Ali pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr. This card is not evidence for the ruling that he did not pledge allegiance. The phrase "six months" is presented as a sentence attributed to al-Zuhri.
sunni.1.grade: Sahih; the phrase "six months" is debated in the commentaries
sunni.2.says: The same event: Lady Fatima's demand for inheritance, Caliph Abu Bakr's reply and Imam Ali's bay'a.
sunni.3.says: The Saqifa debate, Abu Bakr's sermon, Hubab b. Mundhir and Bashir b. Sa'd. The Banu Hashim's holding back and Sa'd's not pledging allegiance are also mentioned. It contains reports from disputed narrators such as Abu Mikhnaf.
sunni.4.says: That Sa'd b. Ubada did not pledge allegiance and later died in the region of Syria. Al-Waqidi's reports are considered weak.
sunni.5.says: The account of the death and of Saqifa; Abu Bakr's saying "I am not the best of you," with a difference in wording.
sunni.6.says: Reports with differing wording about the Banu Hashim's holding back and the process of bay'a. The chains of transmission are mixed.
sunni.7.says: The shura: six men, Abd al-Rahman b. Awf's condition (the Book, the Sunna and the sira of Caliph Abu Bakr and Caliph Umar), Imam Ali's answer "my own ijtihad," and Caliph Uthman's acceptance. It has variants.
sunni.8.says: After Caliph Umar was wounded, he appointed the shura. The detail of the sira condition may not appear in full here.
sunni.9.says: It is the commentary of a Mu'tazili scholar; it is said to contain reports that the sermon exists in early sources.
shia.0.says: Imam Ali describes the caliphate as having been "put on" by Caliph Abu Bakr, himself being at the center like the pivot of the millstone, his being patient with a thorn in his eye and a bone in his throat, and Caliph Umar's leaving the matter to the shura and counting him as one of them.
shia.0.grade: The compilation has no chain of transmission; Sunni critics question its attribution, Shia scholars maintain that it is also found in sources earlier than al-Radi
shia.1.says: Reports on the evidence of the nass of imamate and of the bequest.
shia.2.says: Imam Ali's bay'a and the events after Saqifa, with an imamate interpretation.
shia.3.says: The events after Saqifa and the account of Lady Fatima's house. The attribution of the present copy of the book to Sulaym is disputed; it is not considered evidence on its own.
shia.4.says: The account of the bequest and the imamate. Its attribution to al-Mas'udi is not certain; it is not considered evidence on its own.
shia.5.says: The account of Saqifa, Imam Ali's holding back and the shura. Al-Ya'qubi's school is disputed; Sunni researchers also use him.
disputes.0.title: 19bzxna
What kind of gathering was Saqifa?
disputes.0.sunni: The Ansar gathered at Saqifa, Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubayda came, and the bay'a was taken; the Banu Hashim were not there. In the Sunni reading, this is a consultation held for the good of the Ummah.
disputes.0.shia: The Ansar gathered at Saqifa and the bay'a was taken; there is agreement that the Banu Hashim were not there. In the Shia reading, with the nass at Ghadir standing, this gathering held during the funeral preparations is seen as hasty.
disputes.1.title: ytljen
Caliph Umar's word "falta"
disputes.1.sunni: Caliph Umar called this bay'a a "falta": a sudden matter without consultation. In the Sunni reading, God averted its evil and Caliph Abu Bakr proved worthy.
disputes.1.shia: Caliph Umar called this bay'a a "falta": a sudden matter without consultation. In the Shia reading, this word is haste's own expression in his own tongue; the text is common ground.
disputes.2.title: qopm2g
Imam Ali's delay in the bay'a
disputes.2.sunni: Bukhari ties Imam Ali's bay'a to after Lady Fatima's passing; the report speaks of six months. In the Sunni reading, this is the tension of mourning and Fadak, after which the voluntary bay'a came; there are also reports transmitting an earlier bay'a.
disputes.2.shia: Bukhari ties Imam Ali's bay'a to after Lady Fatima's passing; the report speaks of six months. In the Shia reading, this waiting shows that he stayed in Lady Fatima's grief and understood his place in the caliphate through Ghadir.
disputes.3.title: tixtmt
Lady Fatima's house
disputes.3.sunni: Reports of pressure on those gathered around the house are mentioned in Sunni books. In this reading, the graver details are considered weak or are not accepted.
disputes.3.shia: Reports of pressure on those gathered around the house are mentioned in the sources. Shia books relate graver details; the matter is disputed and varies according to the texts.
disputes.4.title: cnrdgc
The Shiqshiqiyya and the shura
disputes.4.sunni: Caliph Umar left the matter to a council of six; the bay'a was given to Caliph Uthman. In the Sunni reading, Imam Ali's answer is his holding to his own ijtihad; some researchers attribute the sermon to al-Sharif al-Radi.
disputes.4.shia: The shura was formed and the bay'a was given to Caliph Uthman; this is narrated in these sources. In the Shia reading, the Shiqshiqiyya belongs to Imam Ali: he recalls with patience that he did not regard the way of the two caliphs as a condition and that he was counted as one of them in the shura.
questions.0: While the Prophet's family prepared the funeral, the bay'a was taken at Saqifa. How does thinking of standing beside Imam Ali at that hour nourish love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.1: Bukhari ties Imam Ali's bay'a to after Lady Fatima's passing. What does his staying in Lady Fatima's grief during these months tell you?
questions.2: At Saqifa it was said, "The Arabs grant leadership to the Quraysh." What does it remind you of to remember the Prophet's closest family with love alongside this saying?
questions.3: In the Shiqshiqiyya sermon, Imam Ali recalls these days with patience. What do you think his patience adds to the love felt for the Ahl al-Bayt?
summary: While the Prophet's family prepared his funeral, the bay'a was taken at Saqifa. It is narrated in Bukhari that Caliph Umar called this bay'a a "falta." That Imam Ali's bay'a was delayed until after Lady Fatima's passing is also found in Sunni sources (Bukhari, Sahih, no. 4240-4241). In the Shia reading, this day is remembered together with the grief of the Ahl al-Bayt and Imam Ali's place.
key: The bay'a taken while the funeral was being prepared
notes.0: When the Prophet passed away, the Ansar gathered at Saqifa.
notes.1: Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubayda went there too.
notes.2: Bay'a was given to Caliph Abu Bakr; Caliph Umar later described it as a «falta» (Bukhari).
notes.3: Imam Ali and the Banu Hashim were preparing the Prophet's washing and burial.
notes.4: Imam Ali did not pledge allegiance. He stayed silent so that no blood would be shed. Bukhari 4240 relates that after Lady Fatima's passing the people's attitude changed, and in the same hadith it also records the later bay'a. That continuation is not evidence for the ruling that he did not pledge allegiance.
notes.5: According to reports, Imam Ali would give the greeting in the street; people would not return his greeting. This sentence is not Bukhari 4240.
notes.6: According to reports, Imam Ali would go alone to the edge of the well at night and tell of his sorrow and loneliness. This is not a locked page of history.
